Riley (People Ops): Quick note: added a short "calibration + promos" appendix to the OKR & self-review kit. Link: https://redwoodinference.docs/hr/okrs-calibration-2026
Tess (Eng Manager): Nice. Does the appendix change manager responsibilities?
Riley (People Ops): No extra formwork. TL;DR: if you have promo candidates, flag them in the calibration doc, attach 1-2 example outputs, and request a promotion calibration slot. We also added a short rubric for cross-manager alignment.
people-ops-bot: Reminder: self-reviews open 2026-04-01 09:00 UTC; promos intake opens 2026-04-05 09:00 UTC.
Omar (Research IC): Any guidance for research-y goals where impact is stochastic? My experiments sometimes take months.
Riley (People Ops): Good Q. For research: 1) break into milestone experiments, 2) choose proxy metrics (e.g., sample quality delta, reduced eval error), 3) add "risks & unknowns" field in the self-review. Managers should capture tradeoffs in their note.
Tess (Eng Manager): Can we get a micro self-review template tuned for senior ICs with leadership behaviors?
Riley (People Ops): Paste this micro-template for senior ICs:
``
What I shipped (2-4 bullets, include links)
Direct impact (sig figs, figures, or dashboard links)
Leadership/Influence (mentorship, cross-team decisions)
Key tradeoffs, experiments, and learnings
Next quarter focus + 1 leadership or coaching goal
What I need from my manager (clear asks)
```
Priya (Manager): Are managers required to write a calibration note when recommending Exceeds?
Riley (People Ops): Yes for Exceeds and promo recommendations: add a 2-3 sentence calibration note explaining evidence and any cross-team dependencies. Helps reviewers.
people-ops-bot: Calendar event created: "Promotion calibration window" 2026-04-06 10:00 UTC 1: added to people ops calendar.
Omar (Research IC): If someone joins mid-quarter, what's the expectation for OKRs?
Riley (People Ops): For hires <45 days, set 1 ramp goal + 1 contribution goal (small). Managers tag them as "Ramp" in the team roster. There's example language in the appendix.
Tess (Eng Manager): How do we avoid overstuffed Committed goals? Any recommended check?
Riley (People Ops): Quick heuristic: Committed work should fit in a 10-week heads-down plan for one owner. If it requires multiple quarters or >2 full-time people, mark milestones and move to Committed only for the quarter's slice. We added a one-line checkbox in the team copy tool.
Priya (Manager): Rubric snippet please 1: I want something short to paste in our manager notes.
Riley (People Ops): Copyable rubric: 
- Exceeds: Delivered measurable outcomes beyond expectations; clear evidence and impact.
- Meets: Delivered expected outcomes; solid execution and collaboration.
- Needs Improvement: Missed key outcomes or inconsistent execution; manager plan required.
Also add 1 example sentence per level in the appendix.
people-ops-bot: Announcement: anonymous upward feedback form live for this cycle; optional for directs to submit to managers before calibration.
Omar (Research IC): Helpful. For published research or OSS contributions, should we include citations in the review?
Riley (People Ops): Yes please include links and short notes on community impact (stars, downloads, citations) if relevant. That counts toward impact evidence.
Tess (Eng Manager): Last Q: if a manager and IC disagree on rating, what's the flow?
Riley (People Ops): Managers should try to resolve in calibration. If unresolved, escalate to a fast-review panel (people ops + two senior managers) during the calibration window. Document both perspectives in the manager note.
Priya (Manager): Thanks 1: I'll run a ten-minute calibration primer in our team sync and share the one-pager.
